title: Turning Left & Right, Box Junctions
whatItIs: Turning safely is a routine: mirrors, signal, position, speed, look. Box junctions keep crossings clear of queuing traffic.
keyFacts: Turning right: position just left of the middle of the road, or in the lane marked for turning right.
Wait for a safe gap in the oncoming traffic, and don't cut the corner.
Turning left: keep close to the left and watch for cyclists, motorcyclists and pedestrians on your left.
Don't overtake just before you turn left.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT enter a box junction unless your exit road or lane is clear.

keyFacts: You may wait in a box when turning right if only oncoming traffic or other right-turners stop you.

items.title: Mirrors
items.text: Check what is behind and beside you, including bikes on your left.

items.title: Signal
items.text: Signal in good time so others know what you plan to do.

items.title: Position
items.text: Left turn: keep left. Right turn: just left of the centre line.

items.title: Speed
items.text: Slow down to a safe speed for the turn.

items.title: Look
items.text: Look for traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

a.label: Offside to offside
points: Both turn right passing behind each other

b.label: Nearside to nearside
points: Both turn right passing in front
Your view of oncoming traffic is blocked

onTheTest.question: You are turning left into a side road. Who should you watch for most carefully?
options: Cyclists coming up on your left
Vehicles overtaking you on the right
onTheTest.why: Cyclists and motorcyclists can be on your left as you turn. Check your left mirror and blind spot before you turn.

traps: A signal tells others your plan: it doesn't give you priority.
A box junction isn't a place to wait in a queue. Turning right is the only exception.
Don't cut the corner when turning right.
